clue.text: Title-holder has a biography to look at

parts.note: a biography is a life, the written story of someone's life
to peer is to look at something closely

explanation.surface: A titled person has had a biography written about them, worth looking at.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIFE PEER is a member of the House of Lords whose title is not passed on to their heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A peerage held for one lifetime gives its holder a title, so this Lords member is a titled person.

clue.text: Hurt in long row back

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the word for row from end to start

parts.note: a row is a din or racket, a noise

explanation.surface: An injury suffered in a long-running quarrel going back years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' wants to be a line or a quarrel; here it is a din. 'back' turns only that word, which follows L for long.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is a wound or injury to body tissue, a physical harm.

clue.text: Colours available for liquor-jug?

parts.note: a regiment's or ship's colours are its flag
on means available, as in a dish being on the menu

explanation.surface: Asking whether some coloured jug can be had for holding drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel with a handle and spout for serving wine or ale.

clue.text: Gunpowder substitutes by degrees

parts.note: a piece is old slang for a gun or firearm
meal is grain ground to a coarse powder

explanation.surface: Replacements for gunpowder being introduced gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunpowder' must be split into gun and powder, each replaced by a synonym, which is what 'substitutes' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means bit by bit, done gradually rather than all at once.

clue.text: Girl up in Queen Street almost thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters are tossed about and land in a new order
almost means the word Street loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A girl living in Queen Street has nearly been evicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims Street to STREE; 'thrown out' rearranges IN + QUEEN + STREE. 'Girl up' means a girl mounted on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrienne is a female horse rider, a woman sitting high in the saddle.

clue.text: Treacherous sort who haunted "The Eagle"

explanation.surface: A sneaky character who used to hang about at a London pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Pop Goes the Weasel' runs 'In and out the Eagle', the Eagle being a pub on London's City Road.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person, and the rhyme's creature goes in and out of the Eagle pub.

clue.text: Formal order of the dictionary

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is part of the words that follow, taken from within them

explanation.surface: A decree laid down by the dictionary on proper usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official proclamation or decree issued by authority.

clue.text: Live tennis — and from France broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: Tennis shown live, with a French feed being transmitted too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges TENNIS plus ET. 'Live' is an adjective meaning living, not the verb or a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being has feelings and perception, as anything living and conscious does.

clue.text: "Bounty' — sizeable vessel travelling east

parts.note: large is a synonym of sizeable
SS, steamship, is a standard abbreviation for a vessel
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: The Bounty described as a big ship sailing eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bounty is the famous mutiny ship, but here 'Bounty' is generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving of money or gifts, a bounty bestowed on others.

clue.text: Card not quite complete — it makes one spit!

parts.note: a spade is a playing card of the suit of spades

indicators.note: not quite means the word for complete stops short of its final letter

parts.note: full means complete or entire

explanation.surface: A card hand nearly finished, prompting someone to spit in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: A spit is a gardening measure: the depth of earth one spade blade takes, so one scoop makes one spit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's spit is a single spade's depth of soil, the amount lifted in one dig.

clue.text: Portrait-painter depicting first of many wearing eye make-up

indicators.note: wearing means the eye make-up is put on around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: liner is eyeliner, make-up drawn round the eye

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word many

explanation.surface: An artist painting a portrait of someone in eyeliner.
explanation.definitionFit: A limner is an old word for a painter, especially of portraits or miniatures.

clue.text: Schooner, say, departing quickly-it's an artisan's craft

parts.note: a schooner is a large drinking glass for sherry or beer
blowing is slang for leaving fast, as in blowing town

explanation.surface: A sailing schooner leaving fast, with a note on a craftsman's skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schooner' suggests a ship but is a tall drinking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaping molten silica by breathing through a tube is a traditional skilled trade.

clue.text: High sort of layer in duck area

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O
a zone is an area or region

explanation.surface: Something high up found in the area where ducks live.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer is a band of the upper atmosphere high above the Earth.

clue.text: Single girl's best friend?

parts.note: diamonds are a girl's best friend, so one stone set alone in a ring fits; it also suggests a game played by a lone person

explanation.surface: Asking who keeps an unmarried woman company.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitaire is a diamond set on its own, and also a card game for one player.

clue.text: Pluck violins with deepest feeling

parts.note: pluck means courage, which is heart
violins make up the strings section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: Plucking violins with great emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' looks like a verb for playing strings but is a noun meaning courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartstrings are one's deepest emotions, as when something tugs at them.

clue.text: Conscientious, like a churchgoing sort

explanation.surface: Describing someone scrupulous, rather like a regular at church.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a task with religious care means scrupulously; a devout person is pious and faithful.

clue.text: Space-traveller, a carrier of vitamin D

parts.note: vitamin D belongs to the chemical family of steroids, which carry its structure

explanation.surface: A space voyager carrying a supply of vitamin D.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, travelling through space.

clue.text: Perfect whole

explanation.surface: A bare pair of words meaning flawless and entire.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete means flawless or total as an adjective, and entire or undivided.

clue.text: Military band to carry ammunition

parts.note: not a regimental band of musicians but a strap worn across the body by soldiers holding cartridges

explanation.surface: Soldiers' musicians assigned to haul the ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap slung over one side of the torso, such as a bandolier, holds rounds for a soldier.

clue.text: As copper on duty, he provides a service

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the copper symbol comes first

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a duty is a tax or levy, a rate

explanation.surface: A policeman on duty helping people out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal; 'service' is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant clergyman who leads church worship.

clue.text: Hardy comrade filmed in the bay?

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy's friend shown on film at the seaside bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel was Oliver Hardy's comic film partner; the bay tree is also a laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan of the film double act partnered Oliver Hardy, and the sweet bay tree is a kind of evergreen shrub of that name.

clue.text: Poets near collapse in this language?

indicators.note: collapse suggests the letters fall apart and are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Poets about to break down while writing in some tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international tongue created by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Keepsake of priest held in church

indicators.note: held in means the priest is enclosed by the letters for church

parts.note: RC, Roman Catholic, is a crossword abbreviation for a church
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A memento of a priest kept in his church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' is the container signal; RC for a church is a crossword convention, and Eli is the biblical priest who raised Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something kept in memory of a person or past time, a memento.

clue.text: Flat fare from Holland?

parts.note: reads like a fixed travel price but means food from the Netherlands shaped as a flattish round

explanation.surface: A fixed ticket price for travel from the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a Dutch cheese made in flattened wheels, a food from that country.

clue.text: Single valetudinarian dramatist

parts.note: one means single
a valetudinarian is a sickly person anxious about health, so ill

explanation.surface: A lone, chronically sickly playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill was the American playwright of Long Day's Journey into Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene of that surname wrote plays such as The Iceman Cometh, so he is a playwright.

clue.text: This reptile is around no longer

indicators.note: no longer suggests the words is and around cease to stand as they are and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature that has died out and is no longer with us.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes the extinct creature, so 'no longer' reads as plain sense before it is seen as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs were prehistoric reptiles that have been extinct for millions of years.

clue.text: Liquid dose for cow, perhaps, or duck?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cow needs medicine or a dunking.
explanation.walkthrough: A drench is veterinary medicine poured down an animal's throat; to duck someone is to soak them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose of medicine given to livestock by mouth is so called, and to plunge someone into water soaks them thoroughly.

clue.text: Grandmother a sucker for this thin porcelain?

definitions.text: Grandmother a sucker for this thin porcelain?

parts.words: Grandmother a sucker for this thin porcelain
parts.note: plays on the saying about teaching your grandmother to suck eggs, and on a very fine delicate china

explanation.surface: Granny is a pushover for delicate china.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't teach your grandmother to suck eggs' is a British saying: don't lecture someone more experienced.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin, fragile porcelain is named after the shell of a hen's egg.
